title: Microconversation latency vs cost vignette
body:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

This is a compact experimental vignette capturing the latency vs cost tradeoffs for "microconversations" — chat-like interactions dominated by short turns (<= 60 tokens) with occasional longer completions. Purpose: quick collateral for product + solutions to illustrate how model choice, quantization, and small-session batching shape p50/p90/p99 and unit cost. Not intended as canonical benchmark (see linked dashboards) but useful for PRDs, sales one-pagers and internal tradeoff discussions.

KEY TAKEAWAYS (quick):
- Small/short-turn workloads favor smaller models + aggressive prefix/KV caching for cost and p50.
- Quantization gives large unit-cost wins but increases tail in our runtime due to less-optimal kernels for long-token generation and increased bandwidth for multi-GPU splits.
- p99 is strongly correlated with tail concurrency spikes and cache miss rate; reducing cache miss from ~35% -> ~10% cut p99 by ~30-40% on 13B.
- For microconversation semantics, a 13B fp16 variant is the best quality/cost middle ground when tail risks are mitigated with caching and session affinity.

METHODS (sketch):
- Environment: Dedicated cluster (g5-like), 8 workers, clients behind load generator that replays production interarrival distribution for microconversations.
- Workload mix: 65% single-turn short (prompt 20 tokens, gen 40 tokens), 25% multi-turn short (3 turns average), 10% long-turn (gen 150 tokens) to simulate escalation.
- Concurrency profile: base concurrency 12 qps with occasional spikes to 120 qps (10% of time), burst duration mean 18s.
- Measurement: p50/p90/p99 per-request server-side latency (ms), and estimated cost $ per 1k generated tokens (token definitions same as billing layer). All runs use same request size distribution and warm JVM/runtime.

ASCII TABLE: latency (ms) and cost ($/1k gen tokens)

Model                 | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | cost($/1k gen tokens)
----------------------|---------|---------|---------|---------------------
7B-q4 (aggr quant)    | 45      | 110     | 320     | 0.45                
13B-fp16              | 70      | 180     | 600     | 1.90                
13B-q4 (hybrid)       | 60      | 150     | 740     | 0.95                
70B-q4                 | 190     | 520     | 1500    | 6.30                

NOTE: numbers above are from same-day sweep targeting microconversation mix; cost is model-only inference cost estimate (excludes infra overheads like networking & storage). The 13B-q4 example shows lower median latency than 13B-fp16 but higher p99 due to kernel fragmentation and occasional multi-GPU device-sync.

SIMPLE VISUAL (relative tail pressure)
- 7B-q4   : p50-█ p90-██ p99-████ (most stable under burst)
- 13B-fp16: p50-██ p90-████ p99-██████ (higher tail without cache)
- 13B-q4  : p50-██ p90-███ p99-███████ (good median, worse tail)
- 70B-q4  : p50-████ p90-██████ p99-████████████ (expensive and long tail)

ANALYSIS NOTES (working):
- Cache effects: enabling prefix KV cache reduced p50 by ~18ms on 7B-q4 (from 63 -> 45) and cut p99 on 13B-fp16 by ~220ms when hit-rate > 80%.
- Batching window: a 5ms batching window improved throughput and cut cost by ~12% for 7B-q4 without materially raising p90 under baseline concurrency. Under spikes, batching created queuing that enlarged p99 — we need adaptive batching tied to SLOs.
- Multiplex vs slotization: multiplexing small-turns across tokens is efficient for p50 but sometimes hurts p99 when a long generation monopolizes core; slotized reservation reduces p99 at the cost of slightly higher median.
- Quantization trade: q4 variants lower cost but introduce uneven kernel latency; they also increase memory fragmentation leading to occasional OOMs or device-to-device copies when session affinity not applied.

OPEN/UNRESOLVED: (notes to self)
- Need to repeat the 13B-q4 run with new kernel set (PR #317) — early results looked promising but flaky.
- Should instrument request-level cache-miss tagging so we can attribute p99 to miss vs hot-path latency.
- Confirm cost numbers with finance for a conservative $/1k number including carrier and infra (~+14%).

QUICK RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SALES COLLATERAL (one-liners):
- For chatty micro-interactions: recommend 7B-q4 with prefix cache and session affinity; lowest unit cost and best p50.
- For guaranteed conversational quality: 13B-fp16 with canary rollout + cache warmup; better tail when warmed.
- For high-fidelity long-form: 70B family only when SLO budget and cost allowance justify tails — include fallback to smaller variants for spikes.

NEXT ACTIONS:
- (Ethan) run 13B-q4 kernel sweep w/ PR-317 and post updated p99 table by 2028-11-16.
- (Lina) add request-level cache tags to tracing and produce a 1-week heatmap.
- (Samir) draft a 1-page sales snippet with the three recommended profiles + cost bullets.

NOTES: doc intentionally terse. Keep iterations here; once stable, move to product collateral folder and create a slide deck for sales.
